output.summary: Salt-tolerant flowering perennial endemic to Europe, growing wild along mainland European and British coasts. It forms spreading mounds with large fleshy leaves and abundant white flowers. Its blanched stems have been eaten as a vegetable in Britain since around the turn of the 18th century.
output.edibilityNote: Blanched stems are eaten as a vegetable; wild emerging shoots were historically harvested in southern England during early spring.
